text: Photography is a creative art form that utilizes cameras to record images, and a fundamental tool in this process is the shutter. The shutter is a mechanical or electronic device that controls the duration of time the camera’s sensor is exposed to light. This time, known as the shutter speed, determines how much of the scene is captured on film or a digital sensor. As the shutter opens and closes, it allows light to pass through and record the scene as an image. Next, aperture, a variable opening in the lens, controls the amount of light entering the camera. Together, the shutter speed and aperture work in harmony to create the final image, offering photographers the ability to manipulate exposure and depth of field.
